summary.text: Melissa Wells is a Democratic member of the Maryland House of Delegates from District 40 who was first elected in 2018 and has served since January 9, 2019, and she is seeking re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election.
She chairs the Government, Labor and Elections Committee and works as a regional director for the Baltimore-DC Building Trades Unions.

paragraphs.text: Melissa Wells earned a B.A. in political science, law and sociology from the University of California, Riverside, in 2006 and an M.A. in public policy from American University in 2010, according to her General Assembly biography.

She worked as an affordable housing assistant at the Local Initiatives Support Corporation, a policy assistant at the Joint Center for Political and Economic Studies, and a program associate at PolicyLink before becoming regional director of the Baltimore-DC Building Trades Unions in 2015.
Wells served on the Environment and Transportation Committee from 2019 to 2023 and the Ways and Means Committee from 2023 to 2026, where she chaired the Local Revenues Subcommittee in 2025 to 2026.
She was Chief Deputy Majority Whip from 2023 to 2026, chaired the Baltimore City House Delegation in 2025, and in 2026 chairs the Government, Labor and Elections Committee.
Ballotpedia reports that she advanced from the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary.
